GS.rationale: Goldman Sachs is a high-quality franchise with genuine fundamental improvement — Q1 2026 revenue +14.4% YoY, EPS +24.3% YoY, and a blowout Q2 2026 print of $20.98 EPS and $20.34B revenue (39.4% YoY). ROE has recovered to 14.7% with room toward historical mid-to-high teens peaks. AWM scaling past $4T AUM and the consumer banking exit improve franchise quality. However, the market has already priced much of this: P/B expanded 36% (1.9x→2.6x, near top of range), P/E at 17.5x is mid-to-upper range, and earnings yield offers only ~100bps over Treasuries. Balance-sheet leverage has risen to 16.8x assets/equity. The Q2 record is a credible near-term rerating catalyst (Pillar 3), but the magnitude of the beat — GBM +53%, IB fees +55% — signals peak-cycle conditions that may not sustain. Net assessment: solid fundamentals and trajectory (Pillar 1 positive), valuation fair-to-slightly-rich after rerating (Pillar 2 neutral-to-mildly negative), with Q2 earnings as a modest positive catalyst (Pillar 3). Score reflects a quality franchise that is no longer cheap but not yet overvalued.
key_factors: Q2 2026 record: EPS $20.98 vs consensus $14.47 (+$6.51 beat), revenue $20.34B vs consensus $16.22B, GBM revenue +53% YoY, IB fees +55%
AUM crossed $4 trillion for first time; AWM pivot provides recurring fee revenue diversification
ROE at 14.7% (up from 12.0% Jul 2025) still below historical mid-to-high teens cycle peaks — room for further improvement
P/B expanded 36% from 1.889x to 2.571x — near top of 1-year range (2.9x), suggesting bulk of rerating is complete
P/E at 17.47x is mid-range (14.5x–19.6x window); earnings yield 5.7% offers only ~100bps over 10Y Treasury at 4.68%
Balance-sheet leverage increased from 14.2x to 16.8x assets/equity as assets grew $294B while equity was flat
Consumer banking exit (Apple Card) is net positive for franchise focus and capital allocation
GBM cyclicality risk: Q2 surge driven by 53% GBM revenue growth signals peak-cycle conditions
VIX spiked to 20.66 on Jul 29 before settling at 17.09 — elevated volatility near-term benefits trading but increases balance-sheet risk

firmwide net revenues have increased by roughly 60 percent, earnings per share have grown by 144 percent, returns have improved by 500 basis points, and total shareholder return has been over 340 percent, the most in its peer group
